Counsel for Applicant :- Adesh Kumar,Vivek Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
By means of the second bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.88 of 2018 at Police Station-Musajhag, District-Budaun under Sections 498A, 304B IPC.
The applicant is in jail since 13.04.2018.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 18.02.2020.

The following arguments made by Shri Vivek Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
Brijesh Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9930423/

sentences.text: 1. The witnesses have not supported the prosecution case.
Eight witnesses has been examined before the trial court.
At this stage, the Court does not propose to enter into the appraisal of evidence as it might influence the trial.
2. The applicant is a law abiding citizen and had always cooperated with the investigations and joined the trial.
3. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and and shows no sign of early conclusion.
The applicant cannot be faulted for the delay in the trial.
4. Inordinate delay in concluding trial has lead to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant.
The right of the applicant to speedy trial has been violated.
5. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
6. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Brijesh Sharma be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 19.7.2023 Ashish Tripathi  Brijesh Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9930423/
